key_insight: When photovoltaics are assessed for reliable electricity supply rather than panel-level output, firming, storage, and backup drastically reduce net-energy performance and worsen carbon intensity.
engineering_relevance: System designers must account for grid, storage, overbuild, and dispatchable backup constraints, because delivering electricity on demand can cut EROI from strong double digits to near break-even for some firming options.
method: Includes component turnover, grids, storage, renewable overbuild, backup, and fuel supply
Compares unfirmed PV/wind mixes with battery, hydrogen, and gas-firmed supply
evidence_signal: The abstract reports EROI and GWP100 ranges across firming pathways, showing strong degradation from unfirmed renewables to battery, hydrogen, and gas-backed reliable supply.
watch_item: This is an illustrative accounting benchmark, not a simulation or site-specific optimization, so real deployments may perform worse due to non-ideal orientation, curtailment, and delivery losses.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
